overview: This 533-page file traces debates over Japan’s economic recovery under U.S. occupation in 1948. Reports, plans, diplomatic correspondence, and press commentary examine inflation, aid, industrial deconcentration, reparations, trade, and self-support. Regional surveys document labor and political conditions in northern Japan, while British parliamentary extracts extend the file’s scope to wider Far Eastern affairs and Malaya.
interest: Draft recovery plans sit alongside Japanese, American, Soviet, Chinese, and British reactions, revealing competing visions for postwar Japan.
